newsitem.title: HUNGARY: KONZUM OVERHAUL PROMISING, SAYS NEW OWNER.
newsitem.headline: KONZUM OVERHAUL PROMISING, SAYS NEW OWNER.

text.p: A 826 million forints capital injection and a radical overhaul should bring Konzum Rt out of the red next year and revive interest in its shares, the new management said on Monday.
"We would like to rapidly restore confidence in Konzum shares," Laszlo Forczek, Chairman of the board, told a news conference.

Konzum shares were last traded on November 27 at 250 forints compared with a face value of 400 forints, while the Budapest bourse saw an over 2,000 points rise this year to an all-time high above 3,700 points in mid-October.
"Konzum stocks are not demanded at all now, but we hope interest in the shares will renew sooner or later as a result of consistent work," Forczek said.

Forlev Kft, an umbrella firm of the Forczek-led Fordan group of diversified trading and services companies, acquired new Konzum shares representing a 49 percent stake of the increased share capital for 826 million forints in October.
Konzum, formerly a trading and industrial company, by now has retained only its industrial activity.
In the first nine months of 1996 Konzum generated 160 million forints of losses on turnover of 926 million forints and by the end of the year it sees a loss of 200 million.
Fordan began to reduce Konzum's losses and to streamline its activities soon after the ownership structure changed, Forczek said.
As a result, Fordan expects 210 million to 240 million forints in 1997 and 110 million to 220 million in 1998 in freed-up cash, Fordan said in a statement.
For 1997 the Fordan-Konzum group expects a consolidated turnover above six billion forints and slight profit.
"We wish to close the next year in the black with a modest profit as it will be the year of streamlining," Forczek said.
